To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the uncinate fasciculi of young adult females with conduct disorder with comorbid anxiety disorders, and with anxiety disorders alone, show reduced integrity compared with women with no psychiatric disorders.

we found reduced structural integrity of a white matter pathway connecting the amygdala to the orbitofrontal region of the prefrontal cortex, and that this reduced integrity was associated with anxiety traits in the women with only anxiety disorders and with the interaction between poor anger control and high anxiety symptoms in the women with both disorders.

we observed reduced structural integrity of left uncinate fasciculi in women with CD and comorbid anxiety disorder (CD + AD) and in women with anxiety disorder only (AD), but no difference in functional connectivity between amygdala-OFC regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological mechanisms of comorbidity, in particular the overlap of AD and CD.
a group of women who have experienced both conduct disorder (CD) in adolescence and anxiety disorders (with or without CD) in adulthood.
the neural mechanisms of comorbidity, which is a major challenge for the treatment of psychiatric disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amygdala-orbito-frontal structural and functional connection in females with anxiety disorder with and without a past of conduct disorder is not different.
the CD + ANX group had lower structural uncinate integrity compared to the AD-only group and the ND group, but the functional uncinate connectivity was not different between the groups.
the amygdala-OFC circuitry in CD is similar to that in AD, but the circuitry in CD differs from that in ND.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reduced uncinate integrity in females with CD and/or AD is associated with emotion dysregulation, and this is more pronounced among women with CD and/or comorbid AD.
CD is a risk factor for anxiety disorders and the two disorders share similar structural connectivity deficits in the uncinate fasciculi, but not functional connectivity.

the structural integrity of uncinate fasciculi was significantly reduced in both CD + anxiety and anxiety groups, and was associated with anxiety traits in both groups, but was associated with anger and anxiety traits in CD + anxiety group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural correlates of CD are not specific to this disorder, but are also present in individuals with anxiety disorders.

there is a shared vulnerability for CD and anxiety disorders in females that is not accounted for by comorbid psychiatric disorders, and is not reflected in altered connectivity between the amydgala and OFC.
CD is associated with structural abnormalities of the uncinate fascicule in young women, but these are not specific for the disorder.
